label: sparse: copy-phase input e / delimiter, outputting f/o/3/e/x/l (low precision)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.045% of steps). Activation is concentrated in the delimiter step (24% of mass) and copy phase (66%), mostly when the input token is e (50% of mass, 16x lift), and to a lesser degree <DEL>, f, or g. It favours outputs f, o, 3, e, x, l and sequences that start with e. It almost never fires during the original phase or at t<3. The strongest examples are copying the bigram e->f or e->3. Still, every predicate built from these cues has precision under ~9%: the vast majority of e-input copy steps (or e->f/3 steps) do not activate it, and no per-step or history variable I tested separates the active cases. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.24); the top activations are slightly enriched for e->f/3 and late positions, but I could not identify a clear magnitude modulator. Best dev predicate (e->f/3 in copy): P 0.085, R 0.18, F1 0.115.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=9: e, f, g, x; t=13: e, f, x, g; t=11: e, f, g, x) and the token being output, by phase (delimiter step: e, o, x, f; copy phase: f, 3, o, l; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, recall_idx=1, to_go=0.
